chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “One who is killed in the way of Allah is buried in his clothes and is not given ghusl, unless the Muslims reach him while there is still some life in him and then he dies afterward; in that case, he is given ghusl, shrouded, and embalmed with hanut. Verily, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله clothed Hamzah in his garments and did not give him ghusl, but he did perform salat over him.”

key_terms.ثِيَابِهِ: his clothes; the garments in which the slain person is buried
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: a remnant of life; slight remaining vitality before death
key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: performed salat over him; the funeral prayer for the deceased
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; indicating death in a divinely sanctioned cause
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: is embalmed with hanut; perfumed according to funerary practice
key_terms.يُدْفَنُ: is buried; the ruling regarding burial procedure
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: is given ghusl; the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: is shrouded; wrapped in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: Does a martyr killed in the way of Allah receive ghusl and kafan before burial in Shi'a fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one killed in the way of Allah, stating that such a person is buried in his clothes without ghusl if death occurs on the battlefield. If he is found with some remaining life and dies later, then the normal funerary rites of ghusl, kafan, and hanut are performed. The narration also cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with Hamzah as supporting precedent.
